conditions: Any adopted repair of the armour table must enumerate every file that prints each changed value (canon chapter, equipment summary, reference sheet) and apply the change in all of them; a canon-chapter-only edit may not be sealed as the repair.

Any adopted repair must be re-swept over all eight rows on every axis the table prints, with the before-and-after count of strictly dominated pairs reported and zero new pairs required; a repair whose own implied per-DR rate reinstates a domination fails that test.
A body-armour row may not be priced against, or declared dominated by, a build that carries a shield, since the shield stacks with every body-armour row.
The repaired table must price the shared drawback consistently: the same Bane or speed cut may not be discounted at one rung and charged at another.

The column-budget change may proceed on the confirmed rebuild result, but the chosen widths must be shown to fit the binding header of each shrunk column, with the clearance margin reported against the alternative split of the same budget.
point_of_contention: Is the armour table's defect confined to the two duplicate-DR rows, Studded Leather and Half Plate, and may the proposed three-cell repair of that table (Studded Leather DR 2 to 3, Chain Shirt 50 to 20 gp, Half Plate 150 to 60 gp) together with the proposed column-budget change be adopted as scoped?
reasoning: Two refuters independently enumerate the same eight rows on the same axes and agree on the losing set: one reports two strictly dominated rows, names Studded Leather and Half Plate, and excludes Plate because it holds the table's unique top DR; the other reports three strictly dominated pairs that reduce to those same two rows. On that record the defect is real and its footprint is two rows. The round-two challenge to the remedy is unanswered in the record and lands on three points. First, scope: the DR value the repair moves is printed in the canon chapter, in the equipment summary and on the reference sheet, and the prescribing finding's own evidence block concedes the value must be mirrored in both restatements, yet its remedy sentence bounds the whole edit set to one chapter; executed literally, the canon home would read 3 while both restatements still read 2, manufacturing the cross-chapter contradiction the repair was meant to remove. Second, arithmetic: the same challenge rebuilt the book and confirmed the headline count, three dominated pairs before and none after, so the relocation trap did not fire, but it also shows the repaired prices establish a per-DR rate the untouched rows do not honour (the repriced DR-4 row sits 15 gp under the next rung with identical requirement, Bane and speed cut, and the rank is free on one step and 60 gp on the next), and that pricing the untouched quiet row at the repair's own rate reinstates a DR-4 domination; the zero-after result therefore holds only at the one number the repair did not touch. Third, the objection that a shield stacks with every body-armour row is not answered anywhere in the record, and it is accepted. The column-budget finding is partly confirmed and partly not: the independent rebuild closes the table on its own page with all eight rows present, no repeated header, no folio moves and no new wrapping, so both the defect and the direction of the fix are established; but the split offered is justified by the longest value a column holds when the string the shrink must fit is that column's header, and the clearance arithmetic is unexplained against an alternative split of the same budget.
ruling: The council must treat the defect as established but bounded: exactly two rows are strictly dominated, Studded Leather and Half Plate, and no body-armour row may be declared dominated against a build that carries a shield. The three-cell repair may not be sealed as scoped to the canon chapter alone, nor on the arithmetic as offered: every value it changes must be changed in every chapter that prints that value, and the repaired table must carry one consistent price per DR step and one consistent price for the shared drawback. The column-budget change stands on its confirmed effect, that the table closes on one printed page with all eight rows, but the widths chosen must be justified by the binding header string rather than by the longest cell value.

conditions: Replacement casting costs must use the printed prose-count register (Bane, Double Bane, Triple Bane); no numeric Bane translation may be reintroduced.
The Breastplate's recommendation as a caster's armour may stand only with the cost its own row carries: the callout and the row must state the same penalty.
Any dominance claim for a body-armour row must hold the shield count equal on both sides of the comparison.

Both worked examples must be rebuilt from the DR 7 kit baseline, the shield charged exactly once and consistently (in coin or in rank, not both), and the coupled second example's derived figures corrected in the same change.

The weight classes must be assigned so that the class carrying the five-foot cut is exactly the class the chapter calls heavy, with the suit-up-time consequence for the relocated rows accepted and stated.

Where a rule's description and its arithmetic diverge (the Shield Block reaction's raw reduction is larger on the weaker hit than on the stronger one because the missing lower tier is replaced by a fixed 1), the description must be corrected or the rule restated; the two may not ship at odds.
point_of_contention: On chapter 16's own tables, are the armour and casting defects arithmetic (the callout's numeric penalties, the non-convex DR price curve, the Shield Block description) or editorial (prose claims that contradict the stat rows and worked examples priced from an empty inventory), and what is the remedy set?
reasoning: Both findings in this topic agree that the chapter's prose and its stat rows point opposite ways at the same three points, and neither is broken on the arithmetic. The casting defect confirms itself twice over: the callout prices Plate at a numeric figure and the Breastplate at a smaller one while the table one screen above assigns Plate a Triple Bane and the Breastplate a single Bane, and independent dice enumeration puts one Bane 1.7446 points below the 3d6 mean, a Double Bane 2.9302 and a Triple Bane 3.7738, so the printed figures sit about three quarters of a point short of the rows they name, match no printed rung, and are recorded as the exact translation the book's convention forbids while the prose-count form is the live register for spell rolls elsewhere in the book. The second finding is narrowed rather than broken: the Notes cell prices nothing by itself, so the numeric contradiction lives in the callout, but that callout is what escalates a flavour claim into a build recommendation, which is why the recommendation must answer for the uncorrected Bane its row carries. On the price curve the arithmetic is unrebutted: the marginal cost of a DR point falls at one step and two duplicate-DR pairs are ordered backwards, which is what the two dominated rows reduce to; the further claim that Plate is dominated is not established on the same record, because the comparison arms one side with a shield and the other not while the same tables record the shield at +2 DR for 15 gp and cheaper per DR point than every armour row but two, so the measure is the shield rather than the row. The example defect is agreed by both findings and contested by neither: the class kit already supplies DR 7, the printed totals are undercounts, the shield is charged as a purchase the hero already owns, and the second example's derived results move with the corrected baseline. The taxonomy is the one place the two findings differ, one prescribing alignment and the other allowing either cut or alignment; on this record alignment is the direction that costs least, since the two rows already print the speed cut, the class already carries the rule in chapters outside this one, and the only mechanical delta is suit-up time.
ruling: The council must treat both registers as operative and must repair in the tables' register: the spellcasting callout's numeric penalties must be restated as the Bane counts its own table prints (Plate a Triple Bane, Breastplate a single Bane), the Breastplate's promotion as a caster's armour must be reconciled with the Bane that row actually carries, and no numeric Bane translation may replace them. The dominated-row finding stands for the two duplicate-DR rows; the further claim that Plate is dominated is not established, because the comparison arms one side with a shield and not the other. Both worked examples must be rebuilt from the class kit's DR 7 baseline, with the shield charged exactly once, and the coupled second example's derived figures must ship in the same change.

conditions: A class marker must be mirrored in every restatement of the armour table, not only in the canon chapter, and the weight-class vocabulary must gain a glossary headword; a donning-line-only edit may not be sealed as closing this point.
The corrected class list must make the slowed set and the heavy set identical, and the suit-up-time consequence for the relocated rows must be stated where the class is stated.
The worked example must be rebuilt from the class kit's DR 7 baseline, and the shield the kit already supplies must not be charged again as a purchase.
The shield prerequisite exemption must be stated for shields, not only for kit weapons, so that the class whose kit issues a shield can lawfully wield it.
The duplicate prerequisite names (the Discipline abbreviation and the Protection wording) and the collision with the glossary's Protection headword must be reconciled to one term.
The monster-DR comparisons must not be filed as cross-chapter defects: they track the bestiary's Challenge budget, not the armour tables.
point_of_contention: Is chapter 16's armour and shield canon clean across the book, and if not, must the weight-class vocabulary be published where a reader can resolve it, or is a donning-line correction (or cutting the taxonomy) sufficient?
reasoning: Both refuters agree the registration half is clean and the vocabulary half is not, and the counts are verified twice: every armour DR, Discipline and Stealth value and all three shield requirements and bonuses match across the canon chapter, the equipment summary and the reference sheet, armour costs are printed in one place only, and the cross-references to the disciplines and combat chapters and to the glossary resolve. No value set is contested. What is contested is where the repair belongs, and the record favours publishing the class rather than cutting it. The speed-penalty scope is defended rather than narrowed: three chapters outside this one already read the five-foot cut as a property of the heavy class with no member list, and the reference sheet's footnote names the same three rows the table's notes do, so classing the two medium-filed rows heavy makes the slowed set and the heavy set one set of three and stays local to the canon chapter, while the outside uses name the class and need no edit once the members are right. Against that, the registration analysis records that a donning-line-only edit closes the contradiction and neither registration half, because the term carries rule weight in four other chapters while the tables, the glossary and both restatements carry no class at all; it records both arithmetic lists, cutting costing four outside uses and the three notes cells against registering costing the donning edit, one column mirrored across three tables and one headword; and the term is genuinely unlookupable, the glossary's only near-matches being a weapon property and a reaction, with the same prerequisite headed two different ways across facing tables and a glossary headword on that word returning a different concept. The second contradiction is uncontested: no ballot defends the example's empty-inventory baseline, and both sides of the topic agree the class kit already supplies DR 7. The monster-DR lead is withdrawn by its own author, with evidence that the printed numbers track the bestiary's Challenge budget rather than the gear name (same armour printed at different values, different armour at the same value, and the only alignment being a shared ceiling), so it is not a cross-chapter defect.
ruling: The council must treat the canon as not clean but narrowly so: the gear values and the three shields agree row for row across the chapters that print them and may not be revised on consistency grounds alone, while two contradictions stand and must be repaired. The class that carries the five-foot speed cut and the class the book calls heavy must be made the same set, and because that class carries rule weight in chapters outside this one while being registered nowhere a reader can look, the class must be published rather than cut: a row-level class marker mirrored in every restatement of the armour table, plus a glossary headword, since each closes a different half of the gap. The worked example must total from the class kit, and the shield prerequisite exemption must be stated for shields rather than for kit weapons alone. The monster-DR lead is withdrawn and must not be revived as a defect.
